comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PRE-REVIEW VERIFICATION against landed code, plus a SEQUENCING FIX.

CITATIONS CHECKED: completion_sidecar.py:206 and :223 are EXACT (both write model: v.get(model)). plan_review/sidecar.py has drifted — the model field is at :611, not :601 (10 lines, from the S1/S2/S4 changes). Minor, but the plan should cite :611.

SEQUENCING FIX — 2932 (S3) now BLOCKS this story, and the reason is specific to the fact that this payload is SIGNED.

This plan stamps capabilities as the effective record from f184 — i.e. the WHOLE ModelCapabilities dataclass — into provider_provenance. As shipped by f184 that record has THREE fields (native_structured_output, prompt_cache_style, supports_thinking). Story 2932 adds a FOURTH, supports_temperature, because Bedrock hard-400s on temperature for some Claude models and rebars Pass-2 verifiers send temperature=0 (measured: us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 + temperature=0 -> ModelHTTPError 400; without it -> OK).

If this story lands FIRST, the earliest signed verdicts carry a 3-field capabilities object and 2932 then changes the shape of an already-signed payload. That is precisely the argument that got supports_thinking kept on the record in the first place: adding a field after the payload is signed in the field is strictly more expensive than having it there from the first signature. The same logic applies to supports_temperature, so the dependency is now recorded rather than left to luck.

Note this does NOT contradict this storys additive-only / backward-compatible design. That design covers a READER encountering a payload without provider_provenance at all (legacy). It says nothing about the capabilities sub-object gaining a field between two rebar versions that both write it — readers keying on a fixed field set would see drift. Landing 2932 first makes the record complete before anything signs it, so the question never arises.

ALSO CONFIRMED SOUND: the security oracle (base_url with embedded credentials -> persisted endpoint_host is host only, and neither the password nor api_key appears anywhere in the payload) is a genuinely necessary negative control now that dc0d has landed and REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL actually reaches a provider — a credential-bearing URL is a real input shape, not a hypothetical.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PRE-REVIEW BLOCKER — providers.py has ONE line of headroom, and this story's Scope targets it.

After story 2932 landed its bedrock registry entry, src/rebar/llm/providers.py is 299 LOC against the <300 cap that is an ATTESTED acceptance criterion of CLOSED story 7468. This story's Scope says 'src/rebar/llm/providers.py — expose the provenance record from the factory', which cannot be done in one line, so as written this story would breach a signed criterion.

This is the same failure mode that made 2932 unimplementable (runner.py sitting at exactly 800) and it should be resolved in the PLAN, not discovered by an implementer facing an unwinnable constraint. Options, in my order of preference:

(1) Put the provenance assembly in a module with actual room. capabilities.py is 245 LOC and already owns the effective-capability record this provenance embeds, so provenance-from-capabilities is a natural fit rather than a dumping ground. providers.py then contributes only what it uniquely knows (which builder ran, and the endpoint host), via data it already has.

(2) A new leaf module (e.g. src/rebar/llm/provenance.py) alongside bedrock_model.py/capabilities.py, if the assembly is substantial enough to clear the ~100-LOC anti-fragmentation floor. Below that floor it should not be its own file.

(3) Split providers.py — but there is no obvious call-graph seam there yet (it is one class plus three builders), so this is the weakest option and would need its own seam analysis like task 2682 did.

Recommend (1) unless the provenance assembly turns out to be large.

ALSO NOTE for this story's own AC set: runner.py is now 698 LOC. Task 2682's criterion was 'under 700' and the real CI gate is 800, so there is 102 lines of true headroom — but only 2 lines against the stricter target 2682 established. If this story adds to runner.py, say so explicitly and state which limit applies, rather than leaving a reader to assume the 700 figure is still a live constraint.

comments.body:
PRE-IMPLEMENTATION RESEARCH — corrections and constraints found by reading the landed code, before this story is claimed. Several of these change the plan as written.

CITATION DRIFT. The Scope cites `plan_review/sidecar.py:601`; the write site is now **:629** (`"model": verdict.get("model"),` inside `build_payload`, def at :509). `completion_sidecar.py:206,223` are still CORRECT (PASS and FAIL branches; both return literal dicts, so the new key goes in BOTH).

CONSTRAINT THAT CHANGES THE RECOMMENDED HOME. The prior comment recommended assembling provenance in `capabilities.py` because `providers.py` is at 299/300. That still looks right on size (capabilities.py is 277 LOC, the roomiest candidate; runner.py is 698 with only 102 to the 800 cap), BUT capabilities.py is a declared LEAF: its docstring states it imports NOTHING from `runner` or `providers` and keeps `import rebar.llm` stdlib-only. So the assembler there MUST take primitives — `provider: str`, `base_url: str | None`, `caps: ModelCapabilities` — and must NOT take `LLMConfig` or a provider object, or it breaks that invariant. Write the signature that way from the start.

REUSE, DO NOT RECOMPUTE, THE CAPABILITY RECORD. `runner.py:357` already computes `caps = capabilities_for(resolved if self._model_override is not None else model)` once per run, and the object-vs-string distinction there is load-bearing (it was the subject of a prior regression). Provenance must stamp THAT record, not call `capabilities_for` again — a second resolution can silently diverge from the record that actually drove the run.

THE CREDENTIAL ORACLE IS GENUINELY NEW COVERAGE, AND THERE IS A TRAP. No test anywhere in `tests/` exercises a `user:secret@host` base_url. There is also NO existing "URL -> safe host" helper. The correct primitive is `urlparse(base_url).hostname`, which strips userinfo — the same idiom already used at `anthropic_model.py:62-64` and `_mcp_auth.py:270`. THE TRAP: `runner.py:650` uses `parsed.netloc`, which RETAINS `user:secret@`. It is harmless there (a truthiness check only) but it is the wrong accessor to copy into provenance. The test should assert both that the host is right AND that the serialized payload contains neither the username nor the password substring, since `cfg.api_key` also flows near this path.

`tier` HAS NO EXISTING CARRIER. Nothing in the codebase currently expresses first_class vs best_effort. The `"tier"` token elsewhere (`review_kernel/decide.py`, `pass1.py`) is impact-scoring / DET-vs-LLM and is unrelated — do not overload it. This story must DEFINE the field's semantics, which makes it a design decision rather than a read.

SIGNING SEAM WORTH KNOWING. The sidecar payload is NOT what gets signed. Signing binds (ticket_id, manifest), where the manifest is a list of "key: value" strings, and `model` enters via a separate channel: `plan_review/manifest.py:386` and `_commands/transition_close.py:451`. So "the signature still verifies" (this story's collateral invariant) is about the MANIFEST, not the payload — and if provenance is also meant to enter the signed bytes, that is a second, deliberate decision. The precedent for adding a manifest line without invalidating prior signatures is `tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py:285,311` (the rebar-version stamp), and `test_plan_review_resign.py:53-57` has a fake-signer harness that captures the manifest for assertions.

EXISTING COVERAGE TO EXTEND RATHER THAN DUPLICATE. There is no dedicated payload-shape test file. Closest homes: `tests/unit/test_audit_plan_review_v2.py:89` (`test_build_payload_v2_is_observability_only` — the natural extension point for the additive-field claim) and `tests/unit/test_audit_completion_v2.py:85`, which holds the ONLY existing assertion pinning the persisted `model` on a completion payload. `test_plan_review_phase_sidecar.py:10` is the one explicit legacy-payload back-compat test in the tree and is the pattern for this story's "legacy payload without provider_provenance still loads" criterion.

NOTE ON THE 300-LOC CAP: it is NOT encoded in any test or CI gate — I grepped `test_module_size_contract.py` and the provider tests and found no such assertion. It exists purely as the attested AC of closed story 7468, so violating it fails nothing mechanically. That makes it easier to breach by accident, not harder.

comments.body:
GAP 5 — THE WIRING IS INCOMPLETE IN PRODUCTION. Found by the [operator-attested] criterion, which is
exactly what that criterion exists for. This is the most important finding on this ticket.

EVIDENCE: ran a real `rebar review-plan 7a79 --ref HEAD` with the current code live (the worktree venv is
an editable install, so provenance_for IS in the running build). The freshly written REVIEW_RESULT
sidecar contains:
    model               : claude-sonnet-4-6
    provider_provenance : ABSENT
So the field never reaches a production payload, even though all 10 unit tests pass.

WHY THE TESTS MISSED IT: every test hands `build_payload` a verdict dict that ALREADY contains
provider_provenance. That validates the sidecar-write half of the contract and nothing else. The
production question — does the verdict that reaches build_payload ever CARRY provenance — was never
asserted. This is a textbook constructed-input pass: the oracle proved the persist step, not the path.

ROOT CAUSE: there are TWO different verdict objects and only one is wired.
  - `runner.run()` -> `findings.finalize_outcome(..., provider_provenance=...)` (runner.py:372 builds it,
    :611 threads it) produces a PER-CALL result that does carry it. That path is correct.
  - The plan-review GATE verdict is assembled separately by
    `plan_review/orchestrator.py::finalize_verdict` (the dict returned at :604-617, which sets
    `"model": model` at :616). That function's signature is
    `finalize_verdict(ctx, parts, *, coaching, coverage, runner_name, model)` — it receives NO cfg, so it
    has neither `base_url` nor the provider name and cannot assemble provenance today. It simply never
    sets the key, and `sidecar.build_payload`'s defensive `verdict.get("provider_provenance")` then
    writes None.
The same shape almost certainly applies to the code-review gate verdict; verify before assuming.

FIX SHAPE (not yet done): thread provenance into `finalize_verdict` — either accept a
`provider_provenance` argument from the callers that DO hold cfg (workflow_ops / gate_dispatch /
drift_refresh), or pass cfg itself. Prefer passing the already-assembled record rather than cfg, to keep
`finalize_verdict` free of config knowledge and to preserve the "assemble once, carry, never recompute"
rule this story established.

THE MISSING ORACLE: the new test must assert on the verdict produced by the REAL assembly path
(finalize_verdict, or an end-to-end review-plan whose sidecar is then read), not on a hand-built verdict
dict. Written as a RED test first, it should fail exactly as production does today.

STATUS OF THE OTHER FOUR GAPS: (1) persisted-payload credential test — DONE, mutation-verified (.netloc
reintroduces the leak and the test catches it in the PAYLOAD, not just the record). (2) legacy-payload
test — DONE, mutation-verified (.get -> [] raises KeyError and the test catches it). (3)
docs/event-schema.md — DONE, new "Provider provenance" section documenting the field as additive and
optional, alongside the existing session/creation-channel provenance sections. (4) the operator-attested
live evidence — ATTEMPTED, and it is what surfaced this gap; it cannot be satisfied until the wiring
lands. Do NOT close this story until gap 5 is fixed and the live evidence actually shows a populated
provider_provenance.

compiled_state.description:
# S5 — Signed verdicts stamp provider, endpoint, tier, and effective capabilities

## Context / Problem

A signed gate verdict records only a model string. THREE sites write it:
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:629`, `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:206,223`, and
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py:105` each write `"model": verdict.get("model")`. That string is the
resolved `provider:model`, so a verdict produced behind an opaque gateway still claims it came from
`anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`. Once rebar supports two first-class providers and a best-effort tier, a consumer
cannot tell a Bedrock-backed verdict from an Ollama-backed one, even though rebar signs both.

## Approach

Keep the existing `model` string field untouched and **add** a sibling `provider_provenance` object:
`{provider, model, endpoint_host, tier, capabilities}`. `endpoint_host` records the host only (never a full URL,
never credentials); `tier` is `first_class` or `best_effort`; `capabilities` is the effective record from S2
[rebar:f184-a5f1-f181-4700]. Verdicts still sign on every tier — a contributor running Ollama can still exercise
the gates, which matters for the OSS on-ramp — but a consumer now has the lever to reject an off-tier verdict.

Additive-only is deliberate: it makes this a **backward-compatible** payload change, so an older reader ignores
the new key and no store-compatibility capability gate or migration is required. Readers that want the
provenance treat its absence as "unknown, legacy".

**Alternative rejected:** refusing to sign off-tier verdicts. It gives a stronger guarantee but breaks local
development without a first-class provider key, which weakens exactly the contributor on-ramp
`docs/plan-review-gate.md` depends on.

**Alternative rejected:** replacing the `model` string with the structured object. That is a breaking payload
change requiring a compatibility gate and a migration for zero added information.

**Where the record is assembled, and why NOT in `providers.py`.** An earlier draft of this plan said
`providers.py` would 'expose the provenance record from the factory'. That is impossible AND unnecessary:

- IMPOSSIBLE: `ProviderSession.provider_factory` is the `(str) -> Provider` hook handed to pydantic-ai's
  `infer_model`. Its return type is fixed by that contract, so it has no channel to hand anything else back to
  the caller. This is the SAME limitation the module already documents for the retrying httpx client (which is
  why builders append to `self._closeables` instead of returning it).
- UNNECESSARY: `runner.run()` ALREADY holds every field, in one scope — `resolved = _pai_model(cfg)`
  (`runner.py:273`) gives the provider-qualified model, `_provider_name` (`:294`) the provider,
  `caps = capabilities_for(...)` (`:357`) the effective capability record, and `cfg.base_url` the endpoint.
  Nothing needs to travel back from the factory at all.

So the runner assembles the record from data it already has, via a helper in `capabilities.py` (277 LOC, the
roomiest candidate; `runner.py` is at 698 against the 800 cap, so the runner-side change stays a call, not an
inline block). `providers.py` — at 299 against the <300 cap that is an ATTESTED criterion of closed story
7468 — is left untouched, which removes that constraint from this story entirely.

**Reuse the already-computed capability record, do not recompute it.** `runner.py:357` resolves `caps` ONCE
per run, and the model-object-vs-string distinction there is load-bearing (it caused a prior regression).
Provenance must stamp THAT record; calling `capabilities_for` a second time can silently diverge from the
record that actually drove the run.

**`endpoint_host` uses `urlparse(base_url).hostname`, never `.netloc`.** `.hostname` strips userinfo;
`.netloc` RETAINS `user:secret@`. Note `runner.py:650` uses `.netloc` — harmless there (a truthiness check)
but the wrong accessor to copy here. This is the mechanism behind the security oracle below.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — assemble the provenance record. It takes PRIMITIVES
  (`provider: str`, `model: str`, `base_url: str | None`, `caps: ModelCapabilities`) and returns the record.
  It must NOT take `LLMConfig` or a provider object: this module is a declared LEAF whose docstring states it
  imports nothing from `runner`/`providers` and keeps `import rebar.llm` stdlib-only.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — call that assembler and thread the record alongside `ran_model`.
- **`src/rebar/llm/providers.py` is NOT modified** (see Approach).
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — populate it alongside `ran_model`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` (`:629`), `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py` (`:206,223`),
  and `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` (`:105`) — the CODE-REVIEW gate's verdict payload. It was
  missing from an earlier draft of this Scope and is the most consequential of the three for this epic:
  code review is the gate being cut over to Bedrock [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a], so a consumer trying to
  tell a Bedrock-backed LLM-Review vote from an Anthropic-backed one reads THIS payload. Leaving it out
  would have shipped provenance to the two gates that need it least.
- `docs/event-schema.md` — document the additive field.
- `tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py` (new).

## Testing

Contract tier: the mechanism is a producer/consumer shape agreement across a signed, persisted payload, so the
test feeds a real runner result into the real sidecar writer and reads the persisted record back.

- happy path: a Bedrock run persists `provider_provenance.tier == "first_class"` and `provider == "bedrock"`.
- best-effort path: a run with `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL` persists `tier == "best_effort"` and the endpoint host.
- collateral invariant: the pre-existing `model` string field is byte-identical to what it was before this
  change, and the signature over the payload still verifies.
- security oracle (negative control): given a `base_url` containing credentials
  (`https://user:secret@host/v1`), the persisted `endpoint_host` is `host` and the persisted payload contains
  neither `secret` nor the api_key anywhere.
- backward compatibility: a sidecar payload written WITHOUT the new key still loads and verifies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts no credential material from `base_url` or `api_key` appears anywhere in the persisted
      sidecar payload
- [ ] a test asserts a legacy payload lacking `provider_provenance` still loads and its signature verifies
- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar review-plan` on a real ticket writes a sidecar whose `provider_provenance.tier` matches the
      configured provider, shown in the ticket comment
- [ ] `docs/event-schema.md` documents the field as additive and optional
